Local Postgres data lived in an anonymous volume, not in `alkemio_dev_postgres`. `postgres:17` declares `VOLUME /var/lib/postgresql/data`, and quickstart mounted the named volume one level up, so the named volume only ever held an empty `data/` mount point. Any `docker rm`, `down -v` or mount change silently replaced the dev database with an empty one (one machine had four orphaned PG17 volumes, ~2.4 GB, from earlier "lost" databases).

```diff
 postgres:
   volumes:
-    - alkemio_dev_postgres:/var/lib/postgresql
+    - alkemio_dev_postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

Existing setups migrate automatically, once, on the next `pnpm run start:services`:

```text
start:services / start:services:kratos:debug / overmind infra
  .scripts/migrate-postgres-volume.sh
    named volume already holds a cluster  -> "already migrated", no-op
    fresh machine                         -> no-op
    old container on anonymous volume     -> stop postgres, copy into named volume, keep old volume as backup
    old container already gone            -> list dangling PG volumes, refuse: --from <volume> | --fresh
  docker compose up ...
entrypoint-wrapper.sh (anyone running raw `docker compose up`)
  PGDATA holds only the old empty data/ dir -> exit 1 with instructions, never initdb an empty cluster
```

No GraphQL schema change.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `alkemio_dev_postgres` = 8 KB (empty `data/`); the 2.9 GB cluster sat in an anonymous volume. `docker rm` + `up` gave postgres a fresh empty cluster.
  **After:** real run on a machine set back to the old layout (acceptance data, 317 tables):

  ```text
  [pg-volume] moving the Postgres 17 cluster from volume 333173… into alkemio-serverdev_alkemio_dev_postgres
  [pg-volume] stopping alkemio_dev_postgres
  [pg-volume] copied 2.9G
  postgres healthy on alkemio-serverdev_alkemio_dev_postgres, 17.5
  databases / roles / extensions / objects identical; row counts identical except
    synapse cache_invalidation_stream_by_instance +2 (Synapse writes these on every start)
  kratos/hydra/file-backup migrate + hydra-client-setup: exit 0
  re-run: [pg-volume] already migrated
  ```

  |---|---|

  | Re-run | no-op |

  | Raw `docker compose up` before migrating | blocked by wrapper, named volume untouched |

## Summary

Local quickstart stack only (no product code). Since #6650 Traefik publishes the matrix-adapter TCP route on `127.0.0.1:8280` (host tools only), but the Synapse appservice registration `.build/synapse/matrix-adapter.yaml` still pointed at `http://host.docker.internal:8280`. On Linux `host.docker.internal` is the Docker bridge gateway, not loopback, so **every appservice push is refused** and Synapse backs off to 512 s retries:

```
synapse.appservice.api - WARNING - push_bulk to http://host.docker.internal:8280 threw exception(ConnectionRefusedError) Connection was refused by other side: 111
synapse.appservice.scheduler - INFO - Scheduling retries on alkemio-matrix-adapter in 512.000000s
```

Effect: no inbound Matrix event (messages, joins, leaves, read receipts) reaches the server. Comments post without a GraphQL error but never render; conversation subscriptions never fire. Outbound adapter work (room/space create, invites, sends) is unaffected, so nothing errors server-side and the symptom looks like a product bug in whatever feature is being tested. Measured yesterday while running the comment-images acceptance walks (alkem-io/test-suites#684) against a quickstart stack on `develop`: 190–198 refused pushes per 20-minute run, 0 transactions delivered, 10 of 24 walks red purely from this; the same walks are 24/24 on test-alkem.io.

## Change

- `.build/synapse/matrix-adapter.yaml`: `url: http://matrix-adapter:8280` (compose service name on `alkemio_dev_net`), with a comment explaining why the host route cannot work. The file is bind-mounted into Synapse by both `quickstart-services.yml` and `.devcontainer/docker-compose.yml`, and both name the service `matrix-adapter`, so one change covers both stacks.
- `quickstart-services.yml`: two comment lines on the `127.0.0.1:8280:8280` publish saying it is for host tools and that Synapse goes by service name. The loopback publish itself is unchanged (keeps the #6650 hardening).

Docker Desktop (macOS/Windows) is unaffected either way: there `host.docker.internal` reaches the host's loopback, which is why the old URL kept working for some developers.

From inside the running `alkemio_dev_synapse` container on `develop` (adapter v0.8.25):

```
PUT http://matrix-adapter:8280/_matrix/app/v1/transactions/0        -> HTTP 401  (reachable; adapter demands the hs_token, as expected)
PUT http://host.docker.internal:8280/_matrix/app/v1/transactions/0  -> HTTP 000  (connection refused)
```

`docker compose -f quickstart-services.yml config` renders; the registration YAML parses with the new `url`.

To apply on a running stack after checkout: `docker compose -f quickstart-services.yml restart synapse` (Synapse reads the registration at start-up). Because Synapse is already in exponential back-off, the first retry after the restart delivers the queued transactions.

Refs #6614. Split out of #6637, which keeps the delete-path fixes. This PR is only the one-off cleanup of the orphans those leaks left behind.

## Migration — `1790800000000-CleanUpOrphanedRecordsAndPolicies`

One-off and **reversible**. It deletes, in this order:
1. classifications, licenses and profiles that nothing names; their cascading children go with them;
2. the locations and storage buckets owned by the profiles deleted in step 1;
3. every authorization policy that nothing names, including the ones freed by steps 1–2.

Policies go last on purpose. The issue allows any order, and going last also catches the policies that steps 1–2 free.

### Backups and `down()`

Every deleted row is copied whole into `_orphan_cleanup_backup_<table>`. The copy happens in the same SQL statement as the delete, and every part of that statement reads the database as it was before any row is deleted. Three things are copied:
- the row itself;
- the children Postgres deletes with it (tagset, reference, visual, license_entitlement);
- every reference to it that Postgres sets to NULL, kept in `_orphan_cleanup_backup_nulled_references`. Today the only such reference is `file.tagsetId`.

The backups stay in place until the fix is confirmed. `down()` then inserts the rows back parents first, restores each nulled reference that is **still NULL** (one that was set since is left alone), and drops the backup tables.

The backup tables are not counted as names, otherwise the copies would keep the rows they copy. If a table is backed up but missing from `RESTORE_ORDER`, `up()` throws, so `down()` can never silently skip a backup.

**Follow-up:** once the fix is confirmed, a later migration drops the `_orphan_cleanup_backup_*` tables. Only `down()` drops them today.

### Safeguards
- **A row is kept while anything names it:** any foreign key, or any column carrying its id under the conventional name. The migration backup tables, e.g. `_auth_profile_backup_*.profileId`, hold such columns without an FK. Only an explicit list of each table's own cascading children is ignored, so an unknown reference keeps the row, including an owner whose key cascades. If nothing names a table at all, the migration throws instead of deleting every row.
- **There is no generic bucket or location sweep.** The Matrix media staging bucket is named only from configuration (`storage.file_service.matrix_media_bucket_id`). Only buckets and locations whose profile this migration deleted are removed.
- **Files are never deleted.** Their content lives in file-service storage, which only file-service may release. An unowned profile whose bucket holds files is left whole and counted in the log.
- **Rows created in the last day are skipped,** so an in-flight create, which saves children before their parent, cannot lose a child.
- **Only deleted ids come back to Node** (plus a deleted profile's location and bucket ids). Whole rows go from the delete straight into the backup inside Postgres, so ~15k policies' rule JSON is never held in Node memory.

## Dry run on a full dev copy of acceptance data (`up()` → `down()`, rolled back)

| | deleted | after `down()` |
|---|---|---|
| classifications | 2,997 | byte-identical |
| licenses / entitlements | 12 / 106 | byte-identical |
| profiles / locations / storage buckets | 44 / 44 / 44 | byte-identical |
| tagsets / references / visuals | 2,918 / 25 / 13 | byte-identical |
| authorization policies | 15,396 | byte-identical |
| files | 0 | byte-identical |

`up()` took ~14 s. A second run deletes nothing. 12 unowned profile trees whose buckets hold files are left for a file-service cleanup.

Of the deleted classifications, 729 are the live leak since April; the rest are 2025 rows whose policy was never computed, with no owner.

## Tests
- `clean-up-orphaned-records-and-policies.postgres.spec.ts` (10 cases) runs in the CI PostgreSQL job via `pnpm run test:migration:orphan-cleanup:postgres`, which fails rather than skips when `MIGRATION_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset. One case runs `up()` then `down()` and expects every table to come back byte-identical, including a nulled `file.tagsetId`. Removing any one safeguard turns a specific case red; so do dropping the nulled-reference capture and dropping the backup-table exclusion.

## Deploy notes
- Rollback: `migration:revert` restores the deleted rows from the backup tables. The deploy pipeline's gated pre-migration backup remains the last resort.
- Independent of #6637 in either order. Until #6637 ships, the delete paths keep leaking, so some orphans will reappear after this runs.

## Not in this PR
- The policy leaks of the group-A delete paths and failed creates.
- File-bearing orphan trees, historical empty orphan buckets (the 813 in the issue), and orphaned aggregators/documents: these need a file-service path.
- Dropping the backup tables (follow-up, above).

## What was still broken after #6339

QA re-tested #6021 after #6339 merged and acceptance criterion 3 ("same logic applies when the destination's innovation flow was changed via template", the alkem-io/client-web#9353 sequence) still failed: the transferred callout is tagged with one of the destination's **old** state names and shows on no flow tab.

## Root cause (proven at code level)

The transfer logic from #6339 is correct but validates against the destination's flow-state `TagsetTemplate` (`allowedValues` / `defaultSelectedValue`), and that template drifts from the `InnovationFlow`'s actual states through three writers:

1. **Template apply** — `updateCollaborationFromSpaceTemplate` loads the target collaboration with `calloutsSet.tagsetTemplateSet` (eager `tagsetTemplates`, `cascade: true` on every hop). `updateInnovationFlowStates` updates a *separately loaded* copy of the template and saves it; the applier's final `collaborationService.save(targetCollaboration)` then cascades the **stale** in-memory template back over the row, reverting `allowedValues`/`defaultSelectedValue` to the pre-template names. The destination's own callouts stay visible (they are re-homed by state *name*), which is why only transfers exposed it.
2. **Add / delete a single state** — neither `createStateOnInnovationFlow` nor `deleteStateOnInnovationFlow` ever rewrote the template.
3. **Rename** — `TagsetService.updateTagsetsSelectedValue` re-tagged callouts in memory on the rename branch and `continue`d without `save`; nothing cascades to those tagsets, so callouts in a renamed phase kept the old name on reload.

## Fix (behaviour-only; no DDL, no GraphQL change)

- `TemplateApplierService`: re-read the callouts set's `TagsetTemplateSet` after the flow-state update, so the cascade save persists the current vocabulary and template-added callouts are classified against it.
- `InnovationFlowService`: add/delete state rewrite the flow-state template; one shared default rule (`resolveDefaultFlowStateName`: current state while it exists, else first) now backs template apply, rename, add and delete.
- `TagsetService`: persist the re-tag on the rename branch.
- Migration `1789000000000-ResyncFlowStateTagsetTemplates` (data-only, idempotent, no-op `down`): re-derives `allowedValues` from the flow's states in flow order, repairs a missing/unknown default, and moves callout flow-state tags that match no state (case-insensitively) to that default. - `innovation.flow.service.spec.ts` — add-state (incl. sort-order insertion) and delete-state (incl. deleting the current state) rewrite the vocabulary with the shared default rule; two pins for the default rule on the template path.
- `tagset.service.spec.ts` — rename branch saves the re-tagged tagset.
- `src/migrations/__tests__/1789000000000-ResyncFlowStateTagsetTemplates.spec.ts` — structural pins (three ordered UPDATEs, idempotence guards, case-insensitive re-tag, no DDL, no-op down).

## Root cause

Memo signing renders the live Yjs projection and resolves every internal image through document metadata and file-service bytes. Existing memos can still reference a document whose metadata row is absent, or whose metadata exists while the backing bytes return a typed 404. The renderer correctly fails rather than silently changing the signed output, but the existing collaboration migration worker had no memo-image discovery or repair path.

## Fix

- extends the existing one-shot collaboration migration worker with `--repair-memo-images --actor-id <uuid>`; it is a read-only dry run by default, and mutation requires explicit `--apply`
- reads each current memo through the live collaboration room, reports exact missing references and repeated occurrence counts, and only treats typed metadata absence or a typed file-service 404 as confirmed loss
- leaves authorization failures, transport failures/timeouts, 5xx responses, malformed responses, foreign-bucket metadata, and malformed internal locators untouched and reports the memo as failed
- removes only confirmed-missing image nodes from the fresh live Yjs document and persists via the existing correlated durability-barrier path, so concurrent edits are not overwritten by a stale snapshot
- preserves valid/external images and unrelated memo text, formatting, lists, and tables; rerunning a completed repair is a no-op
- reports visual loss explicitly, while the repaired projection is also the projection used by preview/signing

The memo image schema contains no alternate byte source to recover a genuinely absent internal document. Images whose metadata and non-empty file-service bytes are available are preserved.

## Scope
The operator asked for this scope, and it replaces the issue's narrower scope note. This PR builds **screen 01 "Welcome"** from the designer's artifact for the hybrid-app sign-in arrivals `/login?app_signin=required|cancelled|failed`:
- `required` is the screen the app shows the first time someone taps sign in.
- `cancelled` and `failed` are the screens the app returns to after an interrupted attempt. Per the operator, they use the same design with the reason as small text above the buttons.

Every other screen in the design (sign-in form, sign-up, verification) is out of scope. The regular web sign-in and sign-up flows are unchanged.

## Root cause
Each `app_signin` arrival rendered the ordinary `LoginCard` in its `notice` mode, which was built for error-like notices. For the app's own sign-in screen this caused both problems in the issue:
1. The card header's two-column `AuthCardHeader` squeezes "No account? Sign up" into a narrow right column. On an iPhone-width card it wraps over three lines.
2. The notice is drawn as a filled rounded box (`bg-muted`, or `bg-destructive/10` for failed), so "Sign in to continue." looks like an input field.

The app's sign-in screen was reusing an error card.

## Fix
- New presentational CRD component `src/crd/components/auth/AppSignInWelcome.tsx`. It takes props only and fetches no data. It is a full-height column, top to bottom:
  - the enlarged `AlkemioLogo` with the "ALKEMIO" wordmark;
  - the existing `tagline` key as the `h1` (`text-display`);
  - one body line;
  - an optional `message`;
  - then the buttons:
    - **Sign in**: the existing auth CTA style, primary;
    - **Browse public spaces →**: link style, with an arrow icon from lucide.
- The optional `message` is rendered directly above the buttons, centred, as `text-caption` with no background or box:
  - `info` tone: `text-muted-foreground`, `role="status"`;
  - `destructive` tone: `text-destructive`, `role="alert"`.
- `LoginCrdRoute` renders it for every recognised `app_signin` reason:
  - `required`: no message;
  - `cancelled`: info, with the existing `appSignIn.cancelled` copy;
  - `failed`: destructive, with the existing `appSignIn.failed` copy.
  
  Sign in uses the same href the notice card used, `buildOidcRestartHref(...)`.
  
  Browse links to `URL_SPACE_EXPLORER` (`/spaces`), made absolute against the platform origin. That route sits behind `NonIdentity` only, not an auth guard, so anonymous users can open it. It is absolute because this page also renders on the identity subdomain.
- **Create account is deliberately left off this screen**, although the design shows it. Inside the app, the native shell intercepts identity `/sign_up` and always launches `/api/auth/oidc/login`, and the server hardcodes `prompt: 'login'`. The button would therefore land people on the Kratos sign-in screen, not registration. Fixing that is cross-repo work (client-appstore + server) and will be filed as its own story. The web sign-in card's "No account? Sign up" is unchanged.
- A lockout still wins over `app_signin` and keeps the existing notice card, as do the flow-error and Kratos form paths.
- No `isAppMode()` gate: the param is already app-only, and `isAppMode` can be forged on auth paths.
- `AuthShell` / `AuthShellWrapper` get an optional `plain` prop. It drops the decorative dashboard backdrop and stretches the content slot so the welcome view can fill the screen. The footer (Terms / Privacy / language selector) is the shell's existing `Footer`, reused rather than duplicated. Every other auth screen keeps the current default.
- i18n (`crd-auth`, all 6 languages):
  - new `appWelcome.{body, signIn, browseSpaces}` keys;
  - `appSignIn.required` and `appSignIn.action` removed, since nothing renders them any more;
  - `appSignIn.cancelled` and `appSignIn.failed` kept;
  - Dutch keeps "Spaces" untranslated, per the glossary.

### Choices made without asking
- Safe areas: no `env(safe-area-inset-*)` is used anywhere in client-web today, so I did not add any. The 44px bottom padding comes from the design. If the shell's WebView turns out to be edge-to-edge, the insets need a follow-up.
- The design shows the footer as "Terms · Privacy · English". The shared CRD footer also shows Security / About / Support. I reused it as it is instead of building a second footer.

## Regression test
- `LoginCrdRoute.test.tsx`:
  - `required` renders the welcome view with no message and no notice card. It asserts the Sign in href (the OIDC restart) and the absolute browse link, and that no sign-up href reaches the welcome screen.
  - `cancelled` and `failed` render the welcome view with their reason in the right tone and the same Sign in href, and no longer render `card-notice`.
  - The pending `returnUrl` is passed on to sign-in.
  - A lockout wins over `required`.
  - An authenticated `required` arrival still lands on the welcome view (the route-guard exemption).
- `AppSignInWelcome.test.tsx`:
  - the tagline is the `h1`;
  - the links use the given hrefs, the only links are Sign in and Browse (no sign-up), and the browse link is left out when no href is passed;
  - there is no message by default;
  - an `info` message is muted caption text with `role="status"` and no background class;
  - a `destructive` message is red caption text with `role="alert"` and no background class;
  - the message sits directly above the buttons.

## Gates
- `pnpm lint` (typecheck + biome + eslint): passes.
- `pnpm vitest run`: 644 files, 5575 tests pass.
- `pnpm build`: passes.

## What changed

- **Eligibility**: a direct (1:1) conversation is now callable when it has exactly two members and both are users. Group conversations stay callable as before. The guidance conversation, and any 1:1 with a virtual contributor, organization or other non-user actor, stay excluded. All the other conditions are unchanged: the Feature Beta Tester role on the current user, calls configured for the environment, a synced chat session and a resolved Matrix room. The same predicate drives the conversation-list "call active" badge, so 1:1 rows get the badge too.
- **Header**: the 1:1 thread header shows the same CRD `CallControls` (start audio/video) or `ActiveCallIndicator` ("Call active" plus Join with video/audio) as groups, with the same props. A 1:1 still has no group options menu.
- **Intents**: 1:1 rooms open Element Call 0.28 with its direct-call intents: `start_call_dm`, `start_call_dm_voice`, `join_existing_dm` and `join_existing_dm_voice`. Groups keep `start_call`, `start_call_voice`, `join_existing` and `join_existing_voice`. I checked the intent names against the pinned bundle, and a test asserts the bundle configures each one.
- **"Already joined" note**: when the call is already joined in another tab on this device, the note now shows as a tooltip on the "Call active" pill (hover, keyboard focus, or a tap on touch screens) instead of as text beside it. The text beside the pill squeezed the header and wrapped "Call active" onto two lines. The pill no longer shrinks or wraps. As before, no join buttons are shown in that state. This change affects group calls as well.
- **Leave confirmation**: in a direct call it reads "You will leave the call, and it ends for the other person too." The DM intents set `autoLeaveWhenOthersLeft`, so the group wording ("the others can carry on without you") would be wrong there. This is one new key, `call.leaveConfirm.descriptionDirect`, in all six locales.

## Behaviour of the DM intents in the pinned call UI

- The call UI skips its lobby. The camera and microphone start straight away, set by the intent.
- `start_call_dm` sends a `ring` notification event into the room and waits for the other person to pick up. If nobody joins within the ring lifetime, the caller's call ends. That lifetime is the SDK default of 90 s, and Element Call does not override it.
- When one of the two leaves, the call ends for the other.

## Incoming-call signal (no ringing popup yet)

A call you are not in, in any of your 1:1 or group conversations, now shows up with the chat panel closed:

- **Header dot and tab title**: that conversation counts as unread, so the messages dot appears and the tab title gets its "(N)" count. It clears when you join (on any device), when the call ends, or while you are viewing that conversation.
- **Sound**: the chat sound plays once when someone else starts a call in one of your conversations. It keys on the call's own start event (`org.matrix.msc4075.rtc.notification`, sent once by whoever joins an empty call: `ring` for 1:1, `notification` for a group). It follows the chat-sound rules: the chat-sound setting must be on, and it does not play for the conversation you are viewing in a focused tab. Calls from before the page loaded never play it.
- **List order**: a conversation with a call running moves to the top of the chat list, below the pinned one. This applies to calls you are in too, and to groups. When the call ends it falls back to its last-message position.
- Only for Feature Beta Testers where calls are configured, as with the rest of the call UI.

There is still no incoming-call popup with Accept/Decline and no repeating ringtone. The dot and tab title come from the call's participants. The header unread-count query that every user runs is unchanged: the always-on watcher reuses the chat list's own conversations query, only for beta testers and after the same 2 s startup delay. No GraphQL or codegen change.

## No server or infra change needed

The widget capability allow-list already grants sending `org.matrix.msc4075.rtc.notification` / `call.notify` and receiving `org.matrix.msc4310.rtc.decline`. Those are the only extra events DM mode uses, and the call UI's capability request does not depend on the intent. Calls use the same LiveKit and token service, and DM rooms already let members post call state.

Any new usage **fails `pnpm eslint .` and the pre-commit hook**, so it's blocked at commit time. ### [`v2.14.8`](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/releases/tag/v2.14.8)

#### Changelog

Refer to the [2.14 Upgrade Guide](https://docs.nats.io/release-notes/whats_new/whats_new_214) for backwards compatibility notes with 2.12.x. Please note that the 2.13.x version was skipped.

##### Go Version

- 1.26.9 ([#​8740](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8740))

##### Dependencies

- github.com/klauspost/compress v1.20.1 ([#​8737](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8737))
- github.com/nats-io/nats.go v1.53.1 ([#​8737](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8737))

##### Changed

Gateways

- Support for sending and handling the legacy `$GR.` reply prefix, used by servers prior to v2.1.2, has been removed ([#​8615](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8615))

##### Improved

JetStream

- Stalled source and mirror flow control is now reported in stream info and warning logs, making missing `$JS.FC.>` imports or exports easier to diagnose ([#​8633](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8633))
- Stream and consumer placement now prefers peers that have caught up with the metalayer, reducing delays in API responses ([#​8643](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8643))
- Improved the performance of deleting entries from and encoding AVL sequence sets ([#​8646](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8646))
- Fast batch publish now reports backward sequence gaps as well as forward gaps ([#​8699](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8699))
- Stream pending message calculations avoid unnecessary filestore cache access and handle deleted sequence ranges more efficiently ([#​8680](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8680), [#​8681](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8681))
- Stream restore waits for the preferred node to become leader, avoiding an incorrect create response during clustered restore ([#​8690](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8690))
- Memory backed streams avoid copying message headers and bodies twice when storing messages ([#​8652](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8652), contributed by [@​randomizedcoder](https://redirect.github.com/randomizedcoder))

Monitoring

- Leafz now reports whether a leafnode connection uses WebSockets ([#​8683](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8683))

MQTT

- Partial packets are no longer copied in full on every read, reducing allocations and buffer copying ([#​8692](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8692))

##### Fixed

General

- Concurrent account JWT updates no longer invalidate stream imports and interrupt message delivery ([#​8610](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8610))
- Configuration reloads no longer incorrectly disconnect operator mode clients that send an `nkey` ([#​8609](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8609))
- `Connz` requests selecting a connection by `cid` now correctly apply account, user and MQTT client ID filters ([#​8613](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8613))
- Pipelined client operations are no longer processed after a connection is rejected for exceeding the account's `max_connections` limit ([#​8614](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8614))
- Queue subscription deny permissions are now checked against the mapped delivery subject ([#​8616](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8616))
- Outstanding reply permissions are now preserved when inherited account permissions are refreshed without changing the response policy ([#​8620](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8620), contributed by [@​0xasritha](https://redirect.github.com/0xasritha))
- Subscription deny filters are now rebuilt atomically when inherited account permissions are refreshed, preventing a window in which denied messages could be delivered ([#​8622](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8622), contributed by [@​0xasritha](https://redirect.github.com/0xasritha))
- Unquoted configuration values beginning with a number and a size or exponent suffix, such as `0K1abc`, are now correctly parsed as strings ([#​8263](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8263), contributed by [@​koriyoshi2041](https://redirect.github.com/koriyoshi2041))
- Account JWT updates now reject invalid subject mappings instead of reporting success, and failed replacements no longer remove existing mappings ([#​8627](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8627), contributed by [@​vulragrag-star](https://redirect.github.com/vulragrag-star))
- Cached subscription results are now cleared when an already connected client sends another `CONNECT`, preventing stale results from being reused after an account change ([#​8641](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8641), reported by [@​Tan-JunWei](https://redirect.github.com/Tan-JunWei))
- Fixed several data races affecting service imports and exports during configuration reloads and account updates ([#​8675](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8675))
- Per-account routes no longer double count inbound account message and byte statistics ([#​8677](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8677))
- TLS certificate pin validation now checks the correct pins after a configuration reload ([#​8679](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8679))
- Fast batch ping no longer starts a new batch incorrectly ([#​8714](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8714))
- Auth callout rejections are now reported as authentication errors instead of account connection limit errors ([#​8688](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8688), contributed by [@​aniketatgithub](https://redirect.github.com/aniketatgithub))
- Scoped `ProxyRequired` settings are now respected in JWTs and auth callouts ([#​8694](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8694))
- Subscription interest notifications are no longer missed when a subscription is added or removed concurrently ([#​8703](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8703))
- Fixed issues with auth callout `auth_users` bypass
- Fixed a PDH counter buffer overflow on Windows

JetStream

- Stream scale-down requests are now rejected when the target replica count has no configured account tier ([#​8608](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8608))
- Stale per-message TTL entries are now removed when their messages have already been deleted, avoiding repeated expiry scans and excess CPU and memory usage ([#​8595](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8595), contributed by [@​digitalstraw](https://redirect.github.com/digitalstraw))
- The maximum deliveries exceeded advisory is now sent correctly when a consumer's `max_deliver` is lowered below a message's existing delivery count ([#​8605](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8605), contributed by [@​zeke-lin](https://redirect.github.com/zeke-lin))
- The consumer created time is now preserved after recovery ([#​8621](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8621))

- Fixed a race during filestore compaction that could cause consumers to skip messages or lose redelivery tracking ([#​8623](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8623), contributed by [@​as-clearview](https://redirect.github.com/as-clearview))
- Concurrent updates to R1 consumers no longer lose API responses ([#​8628](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8628))
- Stream and consumer create and delete requests received during metalayer catchup now receive responses once catchup completes ([#​8643](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8643))
- R1 consumer create requests no longer lose their responses when the consumer is deleted immediately afterwards ([#​8643](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8643))
- Fixed a data race when handling consumer leader stepdown requests ([#​8647](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8647))
- Fixed a memory leak affecting pull requests and direct gets after a configuration reload when the system account is explicitly configured in the `accounts` block ([#​8650](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8650), contributed by [@​1995parham](https://redirect.github.com/1995parham))
- Fixed a panic when shutting down a clustered JetStream server immediately after startup ([#​8707](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8707), contributed by [@​clwluvw](https://redirect.github.com/clwluvw))
- Idempotent stream create requests with sources no longer time out after leader changes ([#​8703](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8703))
- Recovered ephemeral consumers with `inactive_threshold` set are now cleaned up properly after a server restart ([#​8732](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8732))

Leafnodes

- Publish permissions are now checked against the transformed subject sent over the leafnode connection, avoiding the need to also allow the original stream import subject ([#​8530](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8530), contributed by [@​fbarth-ifr](https://redirect.github.com/fbarth-ifr))
- Fixed incorrect pending byte accounting after a partial compressed write that could stall a leafnode connection and prevent it from reconnecting ([#​8636](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8636))
- Closed leafnode connections are now correctly removed from the account's leafnode list, reducing retained memory and garbage collection pressure ([#​8637](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8637))
- TLS state is now available to auth callouts when leafnodes connect over WebSockets ([#​8686](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8686), contributed by [@​jurry-duty](https://redirect.github.com/jurry-duty))
- Leafnode clients are now shed alongside regular clients during lame duck shutdown, avoiding a thundering herd ([#​8695](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8695))
- Remote proxies now support TLS with `https://` proxy URLs and an optional proxy `tls` block ([#​8701](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8701))
- Remote proxies no longer incorrectly warn that `nats://` URLs are unsupported or lose the hub's initial `INFO` message ([#​8701](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8701))
- Remote proxy options are now rejected when no proxy URL is specified ([#​8701](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8701))
- Leafnode interest and request/reply across account imports ([#​8730](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8730), contributed by [@​edjeffreys](https://redirect.github.com/edjeffreys))

Gateways

This is the biggest nats.go release in a long time: 47 changes with more than half of them coming from 18 external contributors - thank you all!

Most of this release is a robustness effort. Nearly 30 bug fixes address deadlocks, goroutine and timer leaks, data races and stalls in reconnect and drain handling, pull and ordered consumers, async publish and service API. It also adds the `FetchMaxBytes()` option and `Conn.RemoteAccount()`.

JetStream

- Stalled source and mirror flow control is now reported in stream info and warning logs, making missing `$JS.FC.>` imports or exports easier to diagnose ([#​8633](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8633))
- Stream and consumer placement now prefers peers that have caught up with the metalayer, reducing delays in API responses ([#​8643](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8643))
- Improved the performance of deleting entries from and encoding AVL sequence sets ([#​8646](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8646))

- Stream restore waits for the preferred node to become leader, avoiding an incorrect create response during clustered restore ([#​8690](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8690))

Monitoring

- Leafz now reports whether a leafnode connection uses WebSockets ([#​8683](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8683))

MQTT

- QoS2 `PUBLISH` and `PUBREL` processing is now pipelined for increased throughput ([#​8416](https://redirect.github.com/nats-io/nats-server/issues/8416), contributed by [@​levb](https://redirect.github.com/levb))

## Why

The server is being rebuilt behind a new schema. `docs/qa/server-rebuild/plan.md` § W2 makes the client-web Playwright suite the safety net that survives that move, which only works if the schema change touches **one** package: `lib/`. Until now it did not: client-web specs carried their own GraphQL documents through `rawGql` / `adminGql` / `gql` / `gqlAs` / `postGraphqlRaw(document)` / `graphqlRequestAuth({query})` / axios and fetch posts / same-origin `fetch('/api/private/graphql')` inside `page.evaluate` / `page.request.post`, and imported enums straight from the generated schema. This PR is the W2 pre-work that makes the boundary real. It is a pure refactor: no spec gains or loses a case, no assertion changes, nothing a spec clicks or reads changes.

Part of docs/qa/server-rebuild W2 pre-work (PR #693).

## What

### 1. Spec-local GraphQL folded into the lib
- **Inventory** (`grep`/TypeScript-AST over `client-web/src`): **316 inline documents in 63 files** (the audit's 42 had grown with 080/084/086/088/090). Areas: account-deletion 3, authentication 1, callouts 1, classifications 3, contributors-callout 6, form-callout-framing 5, forum-categories 2, helpers 2, language-offer 3, memo-pdf-download 1, messaging-notifications 2, organization-email-invitations 3, organization-space-invitations 3, organization-user-associates 6, platform-roles 6, session-revocation 3, sidebar-widgets 2, space 1, subspaces-callout 5, support-org-community-admin 1, templates-CRD 2, ts7-platform-smoke 1, user-profile 1.
- **Lib**: 81 new documents under `lib/src/scenario/graphql/{queries,mutations}/<area>/` (the house layout; the brief's `lib/src/graphql/` does not exist), **115 new functions** named after the business action in `lib/src/scenario/functions/<area>/<area>.request.params.ts` (me, platform, user, organization, account, space, roleset, callout, templates), exported from the barrel; **15 pre-existing functions reused** (`assignRoleToUser`, `removeRoleFromUser`, `updateCalloutVisibility`, `updateSpaceSettings`, `deleteSpace`, `deleteUser`, `updateUserSettings`, `createPlatformDiscussion`, `deletePlatformDiscussion`, `assignPlatformRole`, `getLicensePlanByName`, …) after widening their `userRole: TestUser` parameter to `GraphqlActor`. 27 existing generated-SDK operations are reused behind new functions (e.g. `MeOrganizationPending`, `GetMeConversations`, `GetUserSettings`, `RoleSetPending*`, `InviteForEntryRoleOnRoleSet`, `submitCalloutFormResponse`, `calloutFormResponses`…); where an existing fragment carried privileged fields (`UserData.email`, `ContributionsData.createdBy.email`, …) a narrow document was added instead, so a non-admin actor reads exactly what the inline document read. Three existing documents were widened additively (`getActivityLogOnCollaboration` +`id`, `communicationsDiscussionData` +`profile.url`, `userSettingsData` +`language`, +`space.collaborationCalloutReaction`).
- **Actor model** (`lib/src/utils/graphql.actor.ts`): every function takes a `GraphqlActor` — a harness persona, `{ bearerToken }` (a disposable user's `getUserToken`), `{ cookieHeader }` (the browser session, routed to `/api/private/graphql` exactly as a `page.evaluate` fetch was) or `{ anonymous: 'private' | 'public' }`. `runAs()` binds the generated SDK to the right endpoint and keeps `graphqlErrorWrapper`'s ENV_FAILURE retry. `client-web/src/functional-e2e/helpers/lib-actor.helper.ts` adds `must(result, what)` and `sessionActor(page)`.
- **Raw documents kept in client-web: none.** The only raw documents left are *inside the lib*, where codegen cannot carry them: schema introspection (`introspectEnumValues`, `introspectSchemaFieldTypes` — graphql-codegen refuses `__type`/`__schema`), the two multipart uploads (`uploadFileOnStorageBucket`, `createCalloutTemplateWithFile`), and the status-returning probes (`readMySessionRaw`, `readMyUserRaw`, `deleteUserRaw`) for the specs that assert on the HTTP status. REST probes (`/api/auth/non-interactive-login`, `id-token-hint`, Kratos admin, MailSlurper, the loopback harness DB) are untouched.
- Two inline probes (`lookupByName { organization(NAMEID) { id } }`, `lookupByName { user(NAMEID) { id } }`) were invalid against the schema (those fields return the id *string*) and always fell into their catch; they now call `getOrganizationIdByNameId` / `readUserIdByNameId`, with the original fallbacks kept.

### 2. Lib-owned enums and types
`lib/src/common/enums/alkemio.ts` re-exports the enums the specs use (`RoleName`, `SpacePrivacyMode`, `CommunityMembershipPolicy`, `CalloutContributionType`, `CalloutVisibility`, `CalloutFramingType`, `CalloutForm*`, `NotificationEvent`, `SpaceLevel`, `SpaceVisibility`, `SidebarWidget`, `ActorType`, `CalendarEventType`, `RoleSetInvitationResultType`, `TemplateType`, `ForumDiscussionCategory`, `SpaceCollectionCardVariant`, `CalloutSelectionMode`, `AiPersonaEngine`, …; `InviteForEntryRoleResultType` from the brief does not exist in the schema) and `lib/src/common/types/schema.ts` the input/result types a spec names. Values are the generated ones today; when the schema changes only these files change. **77 import statements in 61 files** re-pointed from `@alkemio/tests-lib/core/generated/*`, `@alkemio/client-lib/dist/generated/*` and `@alkemio/tests-lib/utils/graphql.*` to `@alkemio/tests-lib` (the barrel now exports `graphqlErrorWrapper`, `GraphQLReturnType`, `runAs`, `GraphqlActor`). Direct generated-SDK calls (`graphqlErrorWrapper(t => getGraphqlClient().Op(…))`, 33 operations) use lib-owned documents and are left as they are — listed in the conventions as the next thing to fold, not a pattern to extend.

### 3. ESLint boundary
`client-web/eslint.config.js`, scoped to `src/**`: `no-restricted-imports` for the three module patterns, `no-restricted-syntax` for `gql` tagged templates and for any string/template literal that spells a document (`query|mutation|subscription …(|{` with a `{` somewhere, or `{ me|lookup|lookupByName|platform|__type|__schema`). The base password/wait/networkidle selectors are hoisted so the `src/**` block spreads both lists (a later flat-config block *replaces* an array rule). **Proof**: reverting `platform-roles/users-admin-actions.spec.ts` to its pre-fold version gives `2 errors (no-restricted-syntax)`; restored: 0. `tests/` (forge-verify's machine-written walks, 4 files with generated imports/inline documents) is outside the contract for now and still lints clean under the base rules.
`.github/workflows/ci-typecheck.yml` gains an **ESLint — client-web lib boundary** step (`eslint "src/**/*.ts" "tests/**/*.ts"`). It is **blocking**: the baseline on `develop` is 0 errors / 43 warnings, and after the fold it is still 0 errors / 43 warnings. Until now only the husky lint-staged hook ran ESLint on client-web.
`client-web/docs/e2e-conventions.md` § 2b documents the boundary.

### 4. Lib contract test
`server-api/src/contract/lib-contract.it-spec.ts` (the lib has no test runner), vitest project `contract`, `@contract` in the describe titles, `pnpm -C server-api run test:contract`. It asserts names and shapes, never server constants: every lib name the client-web specs import (the audit § 3a list, the 115 new functions, `TestScenarioFactory`/`TestUserManager`/`UniqueIDGenerator` statics, the registration chain, the MailSlurper readers), the member names of every lib-owned enum the specs use, the 33 generated-SDK operations still called directly; then `createBaseScenario` (organization + space + subspace + one post callout each) → one read-back per entity type (`readMyUser`, `readSpaceRefs`/`readSpaceAbout`/`readSpaceSettings`/`readSpaceLevelAndVisibility`, `readCalloutFraming`, `readOrganizationRoleSet`, `readRoleSetUsersInRoles`) → `cleanUpBaseScenario`, inside a 60 s budget. **Measured: 10 tests, 13.0 s of test time, 35 s wall clock including the shared global setup** (persona registration) against the local stack.

## Exit gates
- `pnpm --filter @alkemio/tests-lib run codegen` (against the local stack, alkemio-server 0.170.2 — the only drift vs the committed snapshot is the additive `mintMatrixSession`) + `typecheck:native` + `build`: clean.
- `pnpm -C client-web exec tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm -C server-api exec tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `pnpm -C client-web exec eslint "src/**/*.ts" "tests/**/*.ts"`: 0 errors, 43 warnings (all pre-existing).

303 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser
200 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser     <-- flow created TWICE

Runs the nightly `server-api` suite in parallel — **79.2 min → 44.5 min (~1.8×)**, measured on `test-alkem.io` — without weakening a single assertion. All 108 files still run; nothing is skipped,
  deleted or quarantined to gain speed.

  `workspace#040-parallel-nightly-server-api` · story #570

  ## How it works

  The 108-file `nightly` project becomes two projects in the **same** config, run as **one** invocation: `nightly-parallel` (94 files, `groupOrder: 0`, `maxWorkers` from `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS`) and
  `nightly-serial` (14 files, `groupOrder: 1`, `maxWorkers: 1`). Sequential groups give lane separation without a second config or a report merge. The legacy `nightly` project is left **byte-untouched**
  as the rollback surface — reverting is one line in `package.json`.

  Lane membership is **derived, never hand-maintained**: a guard applies hazard rules with name-scoped transitive taint, proves the two lanes partition the nightly scope exactly, and fails closed on
  drift. New spec files default to serial until proven safe — which is how two specs that arrived from `develop` mid-flight were classified with no manual step.

  Three mechanisms protect the signal: **serial-confirm** (any parallel failure is re-run at one worker, and the *serial* verdict is the job's exit code; parallel-fail/serial-pass is logged as
  interference and demotes a file after ≥2 in 7 nights), the **lane guard**, and a **retrospective baseline diff**.

  ## The main finding

  Four static-analysis passes added rules and demoted 22 files, and each run still found interference the rules missed. Two runs on identically fresh databases gave **7 and 63 failures** — same code, same
  data. Every one adjudicated as interference, never a real defect.

  The hazardous pattern is *"assert a shared pool user's privileged action succeeds"* — most of the suite, and not soundly detectable statically. The server compounds it: the `ActorContext` cache is keyed
  by actor alone and **deleted** on any credential change for that actor anywhere.

  So the sharing was removed. **Each vitest worker now gets its own 13 identities** (slot from `VITEST_POOL_ID`; worker 0 keeps bare addresses, worker N uses plus-addressing). Under `pool: 'threads'` a
  worker runs one file at a time, so two concurrently-executing files **cannot** resolve the same identity — structural, not heuristic. On `test-alkem.io` a full run then came back **`exit=0`, 108/108 
  files, 2003 passed, zero failures**.

  This needed a non-obvious fix: `GLOBAL_ADMIN` is granted by the server's bootstrap against the literal `admin@alkem.io`, so per-worker admins were unprivileged and every global-admin scenario failed
  `FORBIDDEN_POLICY`. The harness now grants platform roles per slot at startup using worker 0's bootstrap-privileged token.

  ## Teardown was silently broken

  `cleanUpBaseScenario` wrapped its whole delete sequence in **one** `try`, so the first failure skipped every delete after it. And `deleteOrganization` fails while the account still hosts anything — with
  the org **last**, that failure was invisible. An organisation leaked on essentially every run, of every suite using the factory.

  Measured: wall-clock rose **20.5 → 28.7 min across six consecutive runs**, then dropped straight back to 21.1 when the database was recreated. **~36% of runtime was accumulated residue** — larger than
  every optimisation here combined.

  Teardown is now per-entity best-effort and enumerates what the account still hosts, deleting in the required order (L2 → L1 → L0 → VCs → packs → org). Verified behaviourally: the organisation is
  genuinely gone afterwards, including when an untracked resource was created under its account.

  ## Also here

  - **`uploads.it-spec.ts` is green** — long red because an organisation profile's first visual is an AVATAR, aspect-ratio-locked to 1:1, and the fixture was 410×256. The server was right; the fixture was
  stale.
  - **Environment allowlist guard** — refuses to provision identities against an unapproved host. The Kratos *admin* path bypasses the mail-verification step assumed to protect acc/prod, and this branch
  grows the pool to 13×W accounts with programmatic `GLOBAL_ADMIN`.
  - **Playwright traces no longer published publicly** — one published trace held 73 `ory_kratos_session` entries. They now go to a private 14-day artifact; screenshots and the summary still publish.
  - **Fail-loud worker sizing** — an oversized `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS` aborts naming the variable instead of silently halving the run and reporting green.
  - **Honest mint gate** — it had come to derive its expectation from the code path it polices; now also asserts an independent ceiling, so a duplicate mint can't hide.
  - **Skips never fail the build** — skipped/todo were recorded as failures, so ~59 phantom regressions would have appeared nightly once enforcement was enabled.
  - **Skips must cite a bug** — of 49 unconditional skips, 26 already did; the other 23 are on a closed, dated allowlist that new skips can't join and that fails when an entry goes stale.

  ## Evidence

  | Config | Environment | Wall-clock | Failures | Verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Baseline (CI, W=1) | test-alkem.io | 79.2 min | 2 | — |
  | 69/39, W=5 | test-alkem.io | 56.1 min | 0 | PASS |
  | **94/14, W=5** | **test-alkem.io** | **44.5 min** | 4, all interference | **PASS** |

  `W=10` was tried and failed — setup timeouts and mass-skipped files, one taking 602 s. Resource exhaustion, not interference. **W=5 is the operating point.**

  **client-web verified**: run from this branch against the same environment, it matched the `develop` baseline exactly — 279 tests, 270 passed, 0 failed, the same 2 flaky files, 7 skipped, `exit=0`. That
  exercises the teardown rewrite across its 68 scenario-using files. Its identity path is provably unchanged (`workerCount` defaults to 1; `VITEST_POOL_ID` is never set under Playwright, so slot 0 and
  bare addresses).

  ## Known limits

  - **Notification throughput is a real ceiling.** Parallelism multiplies it roughly linearly with workers; four suites in one day backed up RabbitMQ enough to take the notifications service down.
  - **More server pods will not help** — latency measured identical at rest and under full load; the server idles while the suite runs. The remaining lever is proximity (~43–50 ms RTT from a laptop vs
  ~0.1 ms local). Traefik overhead measured ~0.1 ms.
  - Hazard rules are name/shape blocklists, not structural proofs.
  - The teardown leak summary is **per-worker**, not whole-run — a `worker_threads` consequence; CI greps the whole log.
  - The auto-invite trio's `delay(5000)`-gated assertion is a load-timing hazard: diagnosed, kept serial, not fixed.
  - Mailbox scoping is blocked — MailSlurper has no per-recipient delete, so wipe-all teardown would still race.
  - `callout-reactions.it-spec.ts` interfered once; one entry is below the demotion bar and the ledger surfaces it if it recurs.
  - The ~24 per-area developer scripts consume the changed `lib/` and are **not** covered by this feature's verification.
  - The 23 grandfathered skips are made visible, not fixed — someone still has to do that archaeology.

  ## Raised separately

  - alkem-io/server#6377 — `lookup.*` fields declare `nullable` but throw `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` (37 of 38).
